thread:
maria: quick question — tenant 'acme-ai' hit fallback yesterday and client saw a 500 with zero guidance. Console shows 'route degraded' but no user-facing hint. we need unified mapping + example console copy for rollouts. who wants to take a pass?

aj: can you paste the request/response? last saw an internal 500 from model pool fallback.

maria: repro snippet (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \n -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"summarize...","client_tenant":"acme-ai"}'
```
response:
```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"internal_error"}
```

sean: ok — two things: 1) API should prefer 503 or 424 for upstream failover (not 500), 2) include structured hint header like `X-Redwood-Fallback: model_unavailable;variant=small-v1;reason=capacity` so SDKs can surface guidance.

liang: +1 for 503 vs 500. also propose minimal client-facing message: "service_degraded: request returned a smaller model due to capacity constraints — try again, or contact support for reserved capacity." and add an optional `Retry-After` when we have queueing info.

jess: from console/UX POV: show a banner per-tenant when fallback happens: "Degraded inference (small-v1) is serving requests for your tenant. Some outputs may be lower quality." include link to docs + runbook button. for rollouts we can show canary counts and percent of requests hitting degraded routes.

aj: telemetry checklist: log event `route_fallback` with fields: tenant_id, route_id, fallback_variant, fallback_reason, original_model, latency_ms, client_visible_status (503/424), and sample prompt hash for quality monitoring. ensure we don't log PII.

ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout of "fallback-hint-headers" completed on prod-1 at 2026-03-15T08:12Z :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks. action items: aj to implement header + status change; jess to draft console banner copy & badge; liang to draft SDK-exposure (how to show hint to users) by EOD. assign owners?

aj: assigned aj -> headers/status, PR in staging.

jess: assigned jess -> console copy + badge mockups; will post screenshots.

liang: assigned liang -> SDK behavior + sample code (typescript) for surfacing hint.

maria: i'll update runbook and add tests to gradeboard. small follow-up: should we use 503 or 424 for fallback semantics? pros/cons?

sean: 503 = service unavailable (transient) -> encourages retry. 424 = failed dependency -> clearer when an upstream model pool is the problem. leaning 503 for client simplicity, but we must include explicit hint header so clients know it's degraded vs total service down.

liang: prefer 424 when we absolutely know the original model can't be served and we returned a deterministic degraded alternative; 503 if it's transient and we expect the primary to come back. we should define mapping table in runbook.

maria: agreed. i'll draft mapping table: primary_down -> 424 with hint variant; transient_capacity -> 503 with retry-after when known; quota_exceeded -> 429 with quota-remaining header. will circulate.

aj: quick question — SDKs: do we throw an exception for 424/503, or return successful body with fallback markup? current behavior: we return 200 with model_variant field when fallback is silent. need to standardize.

liang: propose: if fallback returns lower-quality but still successful text, return 200 with `model_variant` and add `X-Redwood-Fallback` header. if we had to stop completely (no variant), return 424/503/429 as appropriate. SDKs should surface a yellow banner (non-blocking) when header present. errors (non-200) should raise exceptions.

jess: that works. i'll design console badge states: green (primary), amber (degraded - variant served), red (failed). copy for amber: "Degraded: outputs may be lower quality; see runbook." link to runbook.

maria: perfect. let's reconvene after PRs. thanks all :rocket:
